newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian minister says frustrated with strong rupee.
newsitem.headline: Indian minister says frustrated with strong rupee.

text.p: India's trade minister said on Tuesday he would like the rupee to weaken and spur exports, but analysts said the long-term solution to sluggish foreign sales lay in more competitive products.
Commerce Minister Bola Bulli Ramaiah said he was frustrated by the value of the rupee, which exporters claim is too strong and makes Indian products more expensive in foreign markets.
"I am not happy, but I have to see the overall situation," Ramaiah replied when asked whether the rupee was at the right exchange rate level against the dollar.
The spot rupee closed steady at 35.81/82 against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday.

Exporters and policy-makers are concerned with the deteriorating trade balance. India reported a $5.44- billion merchandise trade deficit in the 1996/97 fiscal year ended on March, up from $4.54 billion last year.
April exports fell 10.1 percent to $2.52 billion from $2.81 billion a year ago.
Ramaiah said port congestion, infrastructure constraints, a truckers' strike in April and a slowdown in key sectors like gems and jewellery had hit exports.

A strong rupee, fuelled by strong inflows of foreign funds drawn by a soaring stock market and investment opportunties, and confusion over changes in the government's trade policy also hampered foreign sales, analysts said.

Though Ramaiah said merchandise exports rebounded in May, surging eight to nine percent from year-ago levels, growth has remained well below May 1996 levels. In May 1996, exports totalled $2.63 billion, up 13.56 percent over the same month in 1995.
Exporters have been pressing the government to allow the rupee to depreciate to give them a trading advantage and boost overseas sales, which have been relatively sluggish this calendar year.
But the Finance Ministry and Reserve Bank of India fear a falling rupee will fuel inflation. Ramaiah has said that while he would like to see a weaker rupee, other factors must be taken into account.
"Exporters should be competitive, not rely on currency devaluation," said Vipin Aggarwal, chief dealer at DBS capital Trust Securities India Pvt Ltd.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral announced last week creation of a panel to coordinate government policy to bolster exports.
